YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitutions

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

THE OFFERINGS — CHAPTERS 1 THROUGH 7

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 1 The Burnt Offering

1:1 And YHWH called to Moshe, and spoke to him out of the tent of meeting, saying:

1:2 Speak to the children of Yisra'el, and say to them: When any man of you brings an offering to YHWH, you shall bring your offering from the cattle, even from the herd or from the flock.

1:3 If his offering be a burnt offering of the herd, he shall offer it, a male without blemish; he shall bring it to the door of the tent of meeting, that he may be accepted before YHWH.

1:4 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the burnt offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

1:5 And he shall kill the bullock before YHWH; and Aharon's sons, the priests, shall present the blood, and dash the blood round about against the altar that is at the door of the tent of meeting.

1:6 And he shall flay the burnt offering, and cut it into its pieces.

1:7 And the sons of Aharon the priest shall put fire upon the altar, and lay wood in order upon the fire.

1:8 And Aharon's sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces, and the head, and the suet, in order upon the wood that is on the fire which is upon the altar;

1:9 but its inwards and its legs shall he wash with water; and the priest shall make the whole smoke on the altar, for a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

1:10 And if his offering be of the flock, whether of the sheep, or of the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer it a male without blemish.

1:11 And he shall kill it on the side of the altar northward before YHWH; and Aharon's sons, the priests, shall dash its blood against the altar round about.

1:12 And he shall cut it into its pieces; and the priest shall lay them, with its head and its suet, in order on the wood that is on the fire which is upon the altar.

1:13 But the inwards and the legs shall he wash with water; and the priest shall offer the whole, and make it smoke upon the altar; it is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

1:14 And if his offering to YHWH be a burnt offering of birds, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves, or of young pigeons.

1:15 And the priest shall bring it to the altar, and pinch off its head, and make it smoke on the altar; and the blood thereof shall be drained out on the side of the altar.

1:16 And he shall take away its crop with its feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east side, in the place of the ashes.

1:17 And he shall rend it by the wings thereof, but shall not divide it asunder; and the priest shall make it smoke upon the altar, upon the wood that is upon the fire; it is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q25 (4QLevc) is confirmed to cover Leviticus 1-8 (DJD XII, ed. Tov, pp.189-192), and 4Q24 (4QLevb) is confirmed to cover Leviticus 1-3 (DJD XII, ed. Ulrich, pp.177-187). Both are attested for this chapter at PROBABLE level (DJD XII chapter-range confirmed by two independent secondary citations; specific verse-level readings not obtained from primary editions this session). 4Q23 (4QLev-Numa) has very many fragments covering Leviticus; its coverage of this chapter is UNVERIFIED-OPEN at verse level. No confirmed variant reading from any DSS witness for this chapter was obtained this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session. The chapter opens with the rare niphal/qal ambiguity of ויקרא (vayikra) itself in v.1 -- the title of the book -- where the short alef at the end of the word (written small in some MT traditions) is a real, disclosed scribal feature in certain manuscripts of MT, typically explained as indicating that Moshe was called humbly rather than with the full form used of Avraham (Genesis 22:11). This is a well-attested Masoretic scribal tradition, not a textual variant.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The book's governing term קרבן (korban, 'offering/that which is brought near') introduced in v.2 is retained as a transliterated technical term in some traditions; here rendered as 'offering' consistently to preserve English clarity, with the Hebrew disclosed. The repeated ריח ניחוח (pleasing savor/sweet savour) in vv.9, 13, 17 is a formulaic, covenant-ritual phrase throughout the priestly corpus; rendered consistently as 'a pleasing savor to YHWH' rather than varied verse by verse, preserving the formula's own deliberate repetition.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 2 The Grain Offering

2:1 And when any one brings a grain offering to YHWH, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense on it.

2:2 And he shall bring it to Aharon's sons the priests; and the priest shall take from it his handful of its fine flour and of its oil, with all of its frankincense; and the priest shall make its memorial portion smoke on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

2:3 But what is left of the grain offering shall belong to Aharon and to his sons; it is a most holy portion of the offerings of YHWH made by fire.

2:4 And when you bring a grain offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.

2:5 And if your offering be a grain offering baked on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour without leaven, mixed with oil.

2:6 You shall break it in pieces, and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.

2:7 And if your offering be a grain offering of the pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.

2:8 And you shall bring the grain offering that is made of these things to YHWH; and when it is presented to the priest, he shall bring it to the altar.

2:9 And the priest shall lift from the grain offering its memorial portion, and shall make it smoke upon the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

2:10 But that which is left of the grain offering shall belong to Aharon and to his sons; it is a most holy portion of the offerings of YHWH made by fire.

2:11 No grain offering which you bring to YHWH shall be made with leaven; for you shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire to YHWH.

2:12 As an offering of first fruits you may bring them to YHWH; but they shall not ascend to the altar for a pleasing savor.

2:13 And every grain offering of yours you shall season with salt; neither shall you let the salt of the covenant of your Creator be lacking from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.

2:14 And if you bring a grain offering of first fruits to YHWH, you shall bring for the grain offering of your first fruits, fresh ears of grain roasted in fire, crushed grain of fresh growth.

2:15 And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.

2:16 And the priest shall make its memorial portion smoke, of its crushed grain and of its oil, with all of its frankincense; it is an offering made by fire to YHWH.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q25 (4QLevc) is confirmed to cover Leviticus 1-8 (DJD XII, ed. Tov). PROBABLE for this chapter's inclusion within that range; specific verse-level readings not obtained from the primary edition this session. No confirmed variant reading from any DSS witness for this chapter.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 13's 'salt of the covenant of your Creator' (מלח ברית אלהיך) is a distinct covenant-formula phrase, rendered literally; the practice of salting offerings is a real, disclosed ritual requirement running through the priestly corpus, not unique to this verse. Verse 11's prohibition on leaven and honey in fire-offerings is preserved without harmonizing it against the leavened bread explicitly permitted elsewhere in the sacrificial system (e.g., 7:13, 23:17) — the distinction between offering categories is the text's own, not smoothed over here.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 3 The Peace Offering

3:1 And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings: if he offer of the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before YHWH.

3:2 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the tent of meeting; and Aharon's sons the priests shall dash the blood against the altar round about.

3:3 And he shall present of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to YHWH: the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,

3:4 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe above the liver, which he shall take away with the kidneys.

3:5 And Aharon's sons shall make it smoke on the altar upon the burnt offering, which is upon the wood that is on the fire; it is an offering made by fire, of a pleasing savor to YHWH.

3:6 And if his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to YHWH be of the flock, male or female, he shall offer it without blemish.

3:7 If he bring a lamb for his offering, then shall he present it before YHWH.

3:8 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering, and kill it before the tent of meeting; and Aharon's sons shall dash the blood thereof against the altar round about.

3:9 And he shall present of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to YHWH: its fat, the entire fat tail, which he shall take away close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,

3:10 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is by the loins, and the lobe above the liver, which he shall take away with the kidneys.

3:11 And the priest shall make it smoke upon the altar; it is the food of the offering made by fire to YHWH.

3:12 And if his offering be a goat, then he shall present it before YHWH.

3:13 And he shall lay his hand upon its head, and kill it before the tent of meeting; and the sons of Aharon shall dash the blood thereof against the altar round about.

3:14 And he shall present from it his offering, even an offering made by fire to YHWH: the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,

3:15 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is by the loins, and the lobe above the liver, which he shall take away with the kidneys.

3:16 And the priest shall make them smoke upon the altar; it is the food of the offering made by fire, for a pleasing savor; all the fat belongs to YHWH.

3:17 It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q24 (4QLevb) is confirmed to cover Leviticus 1-3 (DJD XII, ed. Ulrich, pp.177-187), placing this chapter within its confirmed range at PROBABLE level; specific verse-level readings not obtained from the primary edition this session. No confirmed variant reading from any DSS witness for this chapter.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] זבח שלמים (zevach shelamim, 'sacrifice of peace offerings') shares its root ש-ל-ם with שלום (shalom, peace/wholeness); this is a real, disclosed etymological connection embedded in the term itself, not asserted as a doctrinal claim. Verse 17's prohibition on eating fat and blood is stated here as a perpetual statute; the fat-prohibition is specific to the categories enumerated in this chapter (suet covering the inwards, kidneys, liver lobe), not a blanket prohibition on all animal fat -- the distinction is the text's own and is preserved rather than generalized.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 4 The Sin Offering

4:1 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

4:2 Speak to the children of Yisra'el, saying: If any one shall sin through error, in any of the things which YHWH has commanded not to be done, and shall do any one of them:

4:3 if the anointed priest shall sin so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bullock without blemish to YHWH for a sin offering.

4:4 And he shall bring the bullock to the door of the tent of meeting before YHWH; and he shall lay his hand upon the head of the bullock, and kill the bullock before YHWH.

4:5 And the anointed priest shall take of the blood of the bullock, and bring it to the tent of meeting.

4:6 And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle of the blood seven times before YHWH, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

4:7 And the priest shall put of the blood upon the horns of the altar of sweet incense before YHWH, which is in the tent of meeting; and all the remaining blood of the bullock shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the tent of meeting.

4:8 And all the fat of the bullock of the sin offering he shall take off from it; the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,

4:9 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is by the loins, and the lobe above the liver, which he shall take away with the kidneys,

4:10 as it is taken off from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make them smoke upon the altar of burnt offering.

4:11 But the skin of the bullock, and all its flesh, with its head, and with its legs, and its inwards, and its dung,

4:12 even the whole bullock shall he carry forth outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire; where the ashes are poured out shall it be burnt.

4:13 And if the whole congregation of Yisra'el shall err, the thing being hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and do any of the things which YHWH has commanded not to be done, and are guilty:

4:14 when the sin wherein they have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bullock for a sin offering, and bring it before the tent of meeting.

4:15 And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullock before YHWH; and the bullock shall be killed before YHWH.

4:16 And the anointed priest shall bring of the blood of the bullock to the tent of meeting.

4:17 And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before YHWH, in front of the veil.

4:18 And he shall put of the blood upon the horns of the altar which is before YHWH, that is in the tent of meeting, and all the remaining blood shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the tent of meeting.

4:19 And all the fat thereof shall he take off from it, and make it smoke upon the altar.

4:20 Thus shall he do with the bullock; as he did with the bullock of the sin offering, so shall he do with this; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.

4:21 And he shall carry forth the bullock outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bullock; it is the sin offering for the assembly.

4:22 When a ruler sins, and does through error any one of all the things which YHWH his Creator has commanded not to be done, and is guilty:

4:23 if his sin, wherein he has sinned, be known to him, he shall bring for his offering a goat, a male without blemish.

4:24 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the goat, and kill it in the place where they kill the burnt offering before YHWH; it is a sin offering.

4:25 And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and the remaining blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering.

4:26 And all the fat thereof shall he make smoke upon the altar, as the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

4:27 And if any one of the common people sin through error, in doing any of the things which YHWH has commanded not to be done, and be guilty:

4:28 if his sin, which he has sinned, be known to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without blemish, for his sin which he has sinned.

4:29 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin offering, and kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.

4:30 And the priest shall take of the blood thereof with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and all the remaining blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar.

4:31 And all the fat thereof shall he take away, as the fat is taken away from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make it smoke upon the altar for a pleasing savor to YHWH; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.

4:32 And if he bring a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring it a female without blemish.

4:33 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin offering, and kill it for a sin offering in the place where they kill the burnt offering.

4:34 And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and all the remaining blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar.

4:35 And all the fat thereof shall he take away, as the fat of the lamb is taken away from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make them smoke on the altar, upon the offerings of YHWH made by fire; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 11Q1 (11QpaleoLeva) is confirmed by named-source citation to cover Leviticus 4:24-26 specifically -- VERIFIED at the level of a confirmed verse-range citation from secondary academic sources this session, though the specific reading was not independently transcribed from the primary Freedman-Mathews edition. 4Q25 (4QLevc, Lev 1-8) and 4Q24 (4QLevb, Lev 1-3, 21-25) do not overlap this chapter's full range; 4Q25's range (1-8) does include this chapter at PROBABLE level. No confirmed variant reading obtained this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The chapter's four-tiered structure -- anointed priest (vv.3-12), whole congregation (vv.13-21), a ruler/nasi (vv.22-26), and a common individual (vv.27-35) -- is a real, deliberate literary structure in the Hebrew itself, with graduated offering requirements (bullock, bullock, male goat, female goat/lamb) corresponding to the offender's social position. This structure is preserved in the chapter division and note placement rather than commented on theologically. Verse 22's נשיא (nasi, 'ruler/prince') is rendered 'ruler' consistently; the term's later technical usage (e.g., post-exilic administrative title) is not read back into this earlier legislative context.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 5 The Sin and Guilt Offerings — Graduated Provision

5:1 And if any one sin, in that he hears the voice of adjuration, he being a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he does not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity;

5:2 or if any one touch any unclean thing, whether it be the carcass of an unclean beast, or the carcass of unclean cattle, or the carcass of unclean swarming things, and be guilty, it being hidden from him that he is unclean;

5:3 or if he touch the uncleanness of man, whatever his uncleanness be with which he is unclean, and it be hidden from him; and, when he knows of it, be guilty;

5:4 or if any one swear clearly with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatever it be that a man shall utter clearly with an oath, and it be hidden from him; and, when he knows of it, be guilty in one of these things;

5:5 and it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that wherein he has sinned;

5:6 and he shall bring his guilt offering to YHWH for his sin which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin.

5:7 And if his means do not suffice for a lamb, then he shall bring his guilt offering for that wherein he has sinned, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to YHWH: one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

5:8 And he shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer that which is for the sin offering first, and pinch off its head close by its neck, but shall not divide it asunder.

5:9 And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering upon the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar; it is a sin offering.

5:10 And he shall prepare the second for a burnt offering, according to the ordinance; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin which he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

5:11 But if his means do not suffice for two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he shall bring his offering for that wherein he has sinned, the tenth part of an efah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense on it; for it is a sin offering.

5:12 And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it as the memorial portion thereof, and make it smoke on the altar, upon the offerings of YHWH made by fire; it is a sin offering.

5:13 And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned in any of these things, and he shall be forgiven; and the remnant shall be the priest's, as the grain offering.

5:14 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

5:15 If any one commit a trespass, and sin through error, in the holy things of YHWH, then he shall bring his guilt offering to YHWH, a ram without blemish out of the flock, according to your valuation in silver by shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for a guilt offering.

5:16 And he shall make restitution for that which he has done amiss in the holy thing, and shall add the fifth part thereto, and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.

5:17 And if any one sin, and do any of the things which YHWH has commanded not to be done, though he know it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

5:18 And he shall bring a ram without blemish out of the flock, according to your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning the error which he committed, though he knew it not, and he shall be forgiven.

5:19 It is a guilt offering; he is certainly guilty before YHWH.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q25 (4QLevc, Lev 1-8, DJD XII ed. Tov) covers this chapter at PROBABLE level. No confirmed variant reading obtained this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] This chapter carries the versification offset documented in the Book-Level Critical Apparatus (Section 4): Hebrew MT's chapter 5 continues through what English versification numbers as 6:1-7 (Hebrew 5:20-26). This project follows English versification (chapter 5 = 19 verses, ending at the guilt-offering summary of v.19); the continuation (Hebrew 5:20-26) appears at the start of chapter 6 below. Directly confirmed this session against Mechon-Mamre's Hebrew-side text, which numbers continuously to 26 verses within a single Hebrew chapter 5.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 1-13 present a real, deliberate graduated-means provision -- lamb/goat (v.6), then two birds if unaffordable (v.7), then a tenth-efah of flour with explicitly no oil or frankincense if that too is unaffordable (v.11) -- a structural feature of economic accommodation built into the sacrificial law itself, preserved in translation without commentary on its social implications. Verse 15's מעל מעל (ma'al ma'al, 'commit a trespass') and v.21's identical construction against a human neighbor use the same root for offenses against the sacred (v.15) and against a fellow person (v.21) -- a real, disclosed lexical parallel the Hebrew draws between the two categories, not smoothed into distinct English vocabulary.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 6 Restitution — The Perpetual Fire — Priestly Portions

6:1 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

6:2 If any one sin, and commit a trespass against YHWH, and deal falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of pledge, or of robbery, or have oppressed his neighbor;

6:3 or have found that which was lost, and deal falsely therein, and swear to a lie; in any of all these that a man does, sinning therein;

6:4 then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was deposited with him, or the lost thing which he found,

6:5 or any thing about which he has sworn falsely, he shall even restore it in full, and shall add the fifth part more thereto; to him to whom it belongs shall he give it, in the day of his being guilty.

6:6 And he shall bring his guilt offering to YHWH, a ram without blemish out of the flock, according to your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest.

6:7 And the priest shall make atonement for him before YHWH, and he shall be forgiven, concerning whatever he does so as to be guilty thereby.

6:8 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

6:9 Command Aharon and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt offering: it is that which goes up on its firewood upon the altar all night to the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning thereby.

6:10 And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen breeches shall he put upon his flesh; and he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.

6:11 And he shall put off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry forth the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

6:12 And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning thereby, it shall not go out; and the priest shall kindle wood on it every morning; and he shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall make smoke thereon the fat of the peace offerings.

6:13 Fire shall be kept burning upon the altar continually; it shall not go out.

6:14 And this is the law of the grain offering: the sons of Aharon shall offer it before YHWH, in front of the altar.

6:15 And he shall take up from it his handful, of the fine flour of the grain offering, and of the oil thereof, and all the frankincense which is upon the grain offering, and shall make the memorial portion thereof smoke upon the altar for a pleasing savor to YHWH.

6:16 And that which is left of it shall Aharon and his sons eat; it shall be eaten without leaven in a holy place; in the court of the tent of meeting they shall eat it.

6:17 It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire; it is most holy, as the sin offering, and as the guilt offering.

6:18 Every male among the children of Aharon may eat of it, as a due for ever throughout your generations, from the offerings of YHWH made by fire; whatever touches them shall be holy.

6:19 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

6:20 This is the offering of Aharon and of his sons, which they shall offer to YHWH in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an efah of fine flour for a grain offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half thereof in the evening.

6:21 On a griddle it shall be made with oil; when it is soaked, you shall bring it in; in broken pieces shall you offer the grain offering for a pleasing savor to YHWH.

6:22 And the anointed priest that shall be in his stead from among his sons shall offer it; it is a due for ever; it shall be wholly made to smoke to YHWH.

6:23 And every grain offering of the priest shall be wholly made to smoke; it shall not be eaten.

6:24 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

6:25 Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before YHWH; it is most holy.

6:26 The priest that offers it for sin shall eat it; in a holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of the tent of meeting.

6:27 Whatever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy; and when there is sprinkled of the blood thereof upon any garment, you shall wash that whereon it was sprinkled in a holy place.

6:28 But the earthen vessel wherein it is boiled shall be broken; and if it be boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water.

6:29 Every male among the priests may eat thereof; it is most holy.

6:30 And no sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place, shall be eaten; it shall be burnt with fire.

VAYIKRA — CHAPTER 16 The Day of Atonement

16:1 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, after the death of the two sons of Aharon, when they drew near before YHWH, and died;

16:2 and YHWH said to Moshe: Speak to Aharon your brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the ark-cover which is upon the ark; that he die not; for I appear in the cloud upon the ark-cover.

16:3 With this shall Aharon come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

16:4 He shall put on the holy linen tunic, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with the linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired; they are the holy garments; and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and put them on.

16:5 And he shall take from the congregation of the children of Yisra'el two he-goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.

16:6 And Aharon shall present the bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself, and for his house.

16:7 And he shall take the two goats, and set them before YHWH at the door of the tent of meeting.

16:8 And Aharon shall cast lots upon the two goats: one lot for YHWH, and the other lot for Aza'zel.

16:9 And Aharon shall present the goat upon which the lot fell for YHWH, and offer him for a sin offering.

16:10 But the goat, on which the lot fell for Aza'zel, shall be set alive before YHWH, to make atonement over him, to send him away for Aza'zel into the wilderness.

16:11 And Aharon shall present the bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and shall make atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin offering which is for himself.

16:12 And he shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before YHWH, and his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the veil.

16:13 And he shall put the incense upon the fire before YHWH, that the cloud of the incense may cover the ark-cover that is upon the testimony, that he die not.

16:14 And he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the ark-cover on the east; and before the ark-cover shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times.

16:15 Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the veil, and do with his blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the ark-cover, and before the ark-cover.

16:16 And he shall make atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleannesses of the children of Yisra'el, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins; and so shall he do for the tent of meeting, that dwells with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

16:17 And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the assembly of Yisra'el.

16:18 And he shall go out to the altar that is before YHWH, and make atonement for it; and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about.

16:19 And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleannesses of the children of Yisra'el.

16:20 And when he has made an end of atoning for the holy place, and the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

16:21 And Aharon shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Yisra'el, and all their transgressions, even all their sins; and he shall put them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of an appointed man into the wilderness.

16:22 And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities to a land which is cut off; and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness.

16:23 And Aharon shall come into the tent of meeting, and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on when he went into the holy place, and shall leave them there.

16:24 And he shall bathe his flesh in water in a holy place and put on his other vestments, and come forth, and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.

16:25 And the fat of the sin offering shall he make smoke upon the altar.

16:26 And he that lets go the goat for Aza'zel shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he may come into the camp.

16:27 And the bullock of the sin offering, and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall be carried forth outside the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.

16:28 And he that burns them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he may come into the camp.

16:29 And it shall be a statute for ever to you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no manner of work, the native-born, or the stranger that sojourns among you.

16:30 For on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins shall you be clean before YHWH.

16:31 It is a sabbath of solemn rest to you, and you shall afflict your souls; it is a statute for ever.

16:32 And the priest, who shall be anointed and who shall be consecrated to be priest in his father's place, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, even the holy garments.

16:33 And he shall make atonement for the most holy place, and he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.

16:34 And this shall be an everlasting statute to you, to make atonement for the children of Yisra'el because of all their sins once in the year. And he did as YHWH commanded Moshe.

[CRITICAL NOTE] עזאזל (Aza'zel), occurring four times in this chapter (vv.8, 10 twice, 26) and nowhere else in the Torah, is retained as a transliterated term rather than translated, reflecting a genuine, unresolved philological dispute: it may function as a proper name (paralleled structurally with יהוה in v.8's "one lot for YHWH, and the other lot for Aza'zel"), or as a descriptive term for the goat's destination or fate ("the goat that goes away" / "complete removal," derived from a root meaning to remove or go away). This reconstruction does not adopt either reading; both are disclosed as live possibilities in the philological literature, and no later interpretive tradition (rabbinic, intertestamental, or otherwise) is treated as settling the question of what MT itself intends by the term. Verse 29's dating (seventh month, tenth day) establishes the calendrical anchor for what later tradition calls Yom Kippur; this reconstruction states only what the verse itself specifies, without importing the later technical name into the translation.
